rationale: C06 supplies the child’s central, concrete policy structure: reject special pay treatment for a limited group within one agency because comparable problems affect other federal employees and should be resolved through coordinated, general legislation rather than agency-specific scales. The child adapts that reasoning to quarantine inspectors, arguing against extending anomalous customs and immigration premium rates and calling instead for rationalized, coordinated compensation across inspectional services. C10 reinforces the broader personnel-management framework and may have informed some surrounding discussion, while C08 presents a weaker parallel of rejecting selective relief pending comprehensive reform.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the premium rates for the customs and immigrant inspectors are so far out of line with prevailing industrial and governmental practice that I do not believe extending their use to other groups of Federal employees would be good management
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I do not believe that this bill represents a sound approach to the problem of recruiting and retaining Government employees. It would have affected only certain employees of one agency
shared_material.explanation: Both reject special compensation machinery limited to a particular federal-employee group or agency as unsound personnel management.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Legislation relating to groups of inspectional employees should seek to improve the overall pattern of premium compensation rather than to attempt to patch the existing uncoordinated pay structure.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the same problem confronts many other agencies, and should be dealt with by general legislation. It would have been a step toward uncoordinated and diverse pay scales for Government employees, when the need is for greater uniformity.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close functional sequence and policy formulation: an agency-specific pay measure would worsen an uncoordinated structure, so comprehensive legislation and uniformity are preferred.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I shall also direct further study of effective means to rationalize and coordinate overtime and premium pay for all inspectional service in relation to that for other Federal employees.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the same problem confronts many other agencies, and should be dealt with by general legislation
shared_material.explanation: The child carries forward C06’s proposed remedy—government-wide or cross-group coordination—while adapting it specifically to inspectional premium pay.
